apollo1|could the test data tell us how.question: Could the test data tell us how the Apollo 1 cabin fire would have behaved?
apollo1|could the test data tell us how.answer: The nearest ISS combustion tests do not cover the Apollo 1 cabin atmosphere (115 kPa, 100 % O₂). The closest tested conditions are still far away, over 20 units in the combined pressure-O₂ space, and no experiment recorded outcomes at that pure-oxygen pressure. Consequently, the test database cannot directly predict flame spread, burn rate, or extinction behavior for the Apollo 1 fire; any inference would be an extrapolation beyond the measured regime. Historical investigations of the accident describe a rapid, uncontrollable fire in a pure-oxygen environment, but the ISS data alone do not provide quantitative behavior for those conditions. [PSI-159] [NASA:apollo_1]
